title_pt: Nada vale mais que a saúde
title_en: Nothing is worth more than health
jp_sentences: 今日は朝から体の調子が悪くて、病院へ行った。
医者の話を聞けば聞くほど、心配になった。
でも、薬を飲んで少し休んだら、だいぶ元気になった。
やはりけんこうほど大切なものはない。
これからは無理をしないで、夜は早くねるようにしよう。
早ければ早いほどいい。
jp: 今日は朝から体の調子が悪くて、病院へ行った。医者の話を聞けば聞くほど、心配になった。でも、薬を飲んで少し休んだら、だいぶ元気になった。やはりけんこうほど大切なものはない。これからは無理をしないで、夜は早くねるようにしよう。早ければ早いほどいい。
translation_pt: Hoje eu não estava me sentindo bem desde cedo, então fui ao hospital. Quanto mais eu ouvia o que o médico dizia, mais preocupado eu ficava. Mas tomei o remédio, descansei um pouco e melhorei bastante. No fim das contas, não há nada tão importante quanto a saúde. De agora em diante eu não vou me forçar, e à noite vou tentar dormir cedo. Quanto mais cedo, melhor.
translation_en: I was feeling unwell from the morning on today, so I went to the hospital. The more I listened to what the doctor said, the more worried I got. But I took the medicine, rested a little, and felt much better. Nothing is as important as health, after all. From now on I won't push myself, and at night I'll try to go to bed early. The sooner, the better.

grammar_target_label.pt-BR: ば〜ほど (quanto mais..., mais...) e 〜ほど...はない (nada é tão... quanto)
grammar_target_label.en: ba~hodo (the more..., the more...) and ~hodo...wa nai (nothing is as... as)

authoring_note: One text: a diary entry written the evening of a sick day, single first-person viewpoint, past tense for the day and volitional for the resolution at the end. Exercises the lesson's two ほど patterns three times: 聞けば聞くほど (proportional), けんこうほど大切なものはない (disguised superlative) and the closing 早ければ早いほどいい. That last line is a real bank sentence (sent:tatoeba-139697) reused verbatim as the closing beat, per spec 1.2. 健康 and 寝る are unlocked as vocabulary in this lesson's cumulative set but 健・康・寝 are not in its kanji known set, so they are written けんこう and ねる, as the hard kanji gate requires.
